meta.title: What Is Resident, and When
meta.subtitle: One component is the whole switch. A section loads in a private world nobody else can see, then arrives all at once

views.label: One component is the switch
views.note: Adding the request component asks for a load. Removing it asks for an unload. There is no other verb.

views.label: It loads somewhere else
views.note: Deserialization happens in a separate streaming world with its own system list, so your world never sees a half-built section.

views.label: Arrival is a move, not a copy
views.note: One bulk move brings the whole section across, which is why entities appear in a single frame rather than trickling in.

views.label: Leaving is a query
views.note: Every entity from a section carries a tag naming it, so unloading is one filtered destroy.

cards.title: Two entities you never authored
items: The scene entity holds the request and a buffer of resolved section entities
One section entity is created per section named in the header
The request propagates from the scene entity down to the section entities unless auto-load is disabled
Section zero is the one that always comes with the scene; the rest can be asked for individually

cards.title: It is deserialized somewhere else on purpose
items: Each in-flight section gets its own world flagged as streaming · Unity.Scenes/SceneSectionStreamingSystem.cs:227
Four stream slots exist by default · :76
That world is populated only with process-after-load systems · :240
System entities are forbidden there, and the code throws if it finds one · :331

cards.title: Arrival is one bulk move
items: The whole section is moved from the streaming world into yours in a single operation · :335
By default one world is moved per update, so arrivals are serialized · :71
That is why a section appears all at once instead of trickling in
And why the frame it arrives on is the expensive one

cards.title: Unloading is a filtered destroy
items: Every entity from a section carries a shared tag naming its section entity
Unload sets that tag as a filter and destroys the matching query · :893, :895
Nothing walks a list of loaded entities; the archetype filter does the walking
Add the request component back and the same section streams in again
